author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Maikel Garcia (hand) to be re-evaluated Tuesday
desc: Maikel Garcia is scheduled to undergo further evaluation on Tuesday to determine a better timeline for his return.
impact: Garcia was placed on the 10-day injured list June 23 after battling a left hand injury for more than a month and opting to rest it so it could fully heal. He has yet to resume swinging a bat, but the Kansas City Royals are expected to provide a clearer timetable for his return after he is evaluated on Tuesday.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jackson Jobe (elbow) to throw live BP Saturday
desc: Jackson Jobe is scheduled to throw a live batting practice session on Saturday.
impact: Jobe began throwing bullpen sessions in early June as he continues to recover from Tommy John surgery he underwent a year ago. He will now advance to facing live hitters and is on track to be activated from the injured list in August.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Janson Junk (shin) to begin rehab assignment Sunday
desc: Janson Junk is scheduled to begin a minor league rehab assignment on Sunday.
impact: Junk has been sidelined since May 28 with right shin bone inflammation. He is expected to pitch three to four innings or approximately 50 pitches in his first rehab start on Sunday. He will likely need at least one additional rehab outing before the Miami Marlins consider activating him from the injured list.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Esteury Ruiz swipes two bags Friday
desc: Esteury Ruiz went 2-for-3 with a walk, two runs scored and two stolen bases in Friday's 4-0 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals.
impact: Ruiz drew his first outfield start since June 21 and showed no signs of rust, reaching base three times and recording a multi-steal game for the second time in June. He owns an impressive .394/.535/.697 slash line with two home runs and eight stolen bases across 33 at-bats this month. He has proven to be worth plugging into daily fantasy lineups whenever he draws the start.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Max Meyer tosses seven scoreless innings
desc: Max Meyer allowed two hits and two walks while striking out five across seven scoreless innings, picking up the win on Friday against the St. Louis Cardinals.
impact: Meyer did not allow more than two runs in any start in June, finishing the month with a 1.78 ERA and 1.15 WHIP with 33 strikeouts across 30.1 innings. He also earned his ninth consecutive winning decision, tying a Miami Marlins single-season record. He'll look to carry that momentum into his next scheduled start on Wednesday against the Colorado Rockies.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Junior Caminero goes yard Friday
desc: Junior Caminero went 1-for-3 with a home run, two walks, one run scored and three RBI in Friday's 6-1 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks.
impact: Caminero followed up Thursday's three-homer performance with a 437-foot three-run home run off Zac Gallen in the first inning. He has been on fire over his last 26 at-bats, posting a .385/.452/.962 slash line with five home runs and 13 RBI.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Cedric Mullins II launches homer Friday
desc: Cedric Mullins II went 1-for-4 with a solo home run in Friday's 6-1 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks.
impact: Mullins hit a 433-foot home run off Zac Gallen in the seventh inning to give the Tampa Bay Rays a 4-1 lead. He has now recorded a hit in each of his last six starts and owns a .258/.361/.452 slash line across 62 at-bats in June.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Nick Martinez picks up win Friday
desc: Nick Martinez allowed one run on six hits and no walks while striking out three across 5.2 innings in Friday's 6-1 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks.
impact: Martinez snapped a streak of four straight outings allowing three or more earned runs with an impressive one-run performance, picking up the win in the process. While he finished June with a 5.14 ERA and 1.25 WHIP across five starts, he closed the month on a high note and still owns an impressive 2.66 ERA and 1.15 WHIP on the season. He'll look to carry that momentum into July in his next scheduled start on Thursday against the Kansas City Royals.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Colin Rea provides Cubs with strong outing Friday
desc: Colin Rea allowed one run on five hits and three walks while striking out four across five innings in Friday's 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers.
impact: Rea tossed five scoreless innings before running into trouble in the sixth, surrendering a single and a walk before being lifted for Ethan Roberts, who allowed one of those runners to score. After giving up 13 runs across his first three starts of June, Rea has turned things around over his last two outings, allowing just one run across 10.1 innings. His next scheduled start is on Friday against the St. Louis Cardinals.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Seiya Suzuki hits solo shot Friday
desc: Seiya Suzuki went 1-for-2 with a home run, one walk, one run scored and two RBI in Friday's 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers.
impact: Suzuki hit a 409-foot solo homer off Jacob Misiorowski in the fifth inning, snapping a 49 plate appearance homerless drought dating back to June 11. The blast also ended a two-game hitless streak, giving him his fourth home run of the month. In June, he owns an impressive .300/.398/.543 slash line.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Ty France hits home run Friday
desc: Ty France went 1-for-2 with a home run and three RBI in the Padres 7-1 win over the Dodgers on Friday.
impact: After falling behind 1-0 early, France put San Diego ahead with a three-run home run off Roki Sasaki. He is officially up to double digit blasts on the season.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Walker Buehler defeats former team Friday
desc: Walker Buehler allowed one run on three hits over 5 1/3 innings with five strikeouts and three walks in a win on Friday against the Dodgers.
impact: Buehler allowed a solo home run to Mookie Betts in the second inning with that being the lone damage. He allowed just two other hits on the night, pitching into the sixth inning against his former team. He'll face the Cubs next.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Geraldo Perdomo hits home run Friday
desc: Geraldo Perdomo went 2-for-4 with a home run in the Diamondbacks 6-1 loss against the Rays on Friday.
impact: Perdomo opened the game's scoring with a solo blast in the first inning. That would be the only run scored on the night by Arizona.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Zac Gallen takes loss Friday
desc: Zac Gallen allowed five runs on four hits over 6 2/3 innings with two walks in a loss on Friday against the Rays.
impact: It didn't take long for Gallen to get himself in trouble as a walk and hit batter to open the bottom of the first was followed by a three-run blast hit by Junior Caminero. He was able to settle in enough to pitch into the seventh inning, but he still allowed five runs and took the loss. He'll face the Giants next.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Esmerlyn Valdez goes yard Friday
desc: Esmerlyn Valdez went 2-for-4 with a home run in the Pirates 6-4 loss on Friday against the Reds.
impact: Valdez and Marcell Ozuna both went yard in the sixth inning to tie the game. It was his third long ball of the season.
